facts.detail: American envoys traveled to France seeking to buy a single port city.
The envoys unexpectedly secured the entire surrounding territory for a similar cost.
A brief truce halted conflict between French and British forces in 1802.
French leadership held massive North American lands with plans to rebuild a western empire.
The core of French imperial strategy rested on Saint-Domingue, its wealthiest Caribbean island.
The island generated massive wealth through sugar and coffee produced by forced labor.
An uprising by the forced workers broke French control over the territory.
During the European peace, French troops were sent to suppress the island revolt.
Outbreaks of yellow fever decimated the invading force, resulting in permanent defeat.
Without the Caribbean colony, holding vast mainland territory lost strategic value.
American commerce depended heavily on river transport through French-controlled New Orleans.
In 1803, American leadership authorized a ten million dollar offer for the port city.
Threatened by renewed war and cash shortages, French leaders sought to shed distant lands.
French leaders countered by offering the complete territory for fifteen million dollars.
The delegates accepted the surprise proposal despite lacking formal authorization.
The deal expanded American borders dramatically at roughly four cents per acre.
